title: LumenDocs hosted embeddings + rerank search relevance demo
summary: AE+SE walked LumenDocs through Redwood's hosted embeddings and reranking endpoints focusing on improving search relevance for long-form docs. Demo covered API calls, Console search tuning, Optimize suggestions for batching and cache, cost/latency tradeoffs, and security questions (SOC2, data retention, KMS). Agreed to run a 2-week pilot: Redwood will send guidance + sample benchmark notebook; customer to provide 1k query set and sample corpus.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood Solutions), Riya (LumenDocs), Ben (LumenDocs ML), Tara (LumenDocs Product), Samir (Infra), Olga (Data)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Quick hosted API demo for embeddings + reranker; emphasis on improving result relevance for long docs and maintaining low latency.

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we have about an hour, quick agenda — show our hosted embeddings endpoint, then the rerank endpoint, demo a live relevance tuning flow in Console and then cover Optimize recommendations and security. Any additions?
[00:12] Riya: That sounds great. We're primarily focused on improving recall for long technical docs and reducing noise at top-5. Latency under 180ms median is ideal for our UI.
[00:22] Ben: Also want to keep costs predictable, we run a lot of nightly batch indexing jobs.
[00:27] Marco: Cool. I'll share my screen and start with the embeddings API — two endpoints: /v1/embeddings and /v1/rerank. Example request: POST /v1/embeddings with model param redwood-embed-002, payload is text or batch of texts, returns vectors.
[00:45] Marco: (typing) demo: sending a batch of 50 doc chunks. Note: our hosting supports streaming for large payloads and automatic batching on the server-side to amortize token cost.
[01:12] Ben: Does server-side batching affect latency for individual requests? We want sub-200ms median.
[01:20] Marco: Good q — we have adaptive batching. For low concurrency we prioritize latency, for high throughput batches are aggregated small windows (10-25ms) — you can set max latency in the route config. Optimize will also recommend per-workload batch windows.
[01:35] Sofia: Important to call out hosted vs dedicated — hosted gives the fastest time-to-value and simple integration; dedicated gives predictable throughput if you need strict SLOs. For your workloads, you might start hosted for the pilot and later move to Dedicated if throughput grows.
[02:00] Tara: Can you show the rerank flow? How does rerank interact with our existing BM25 + vector combo?
[02:07] Marco: Sure. Typical pattern: run an initial retrieval (BM25 or vector similarity) to produce top-N candidates, then call /v1/rerank with the query + candidate list. The reranker scores each candidate for final sort. It can take semantic features and structured fields.
[02:32] Marco: Demo: I call rerank with our sample query 'how to configure tls for ingestion pipeline' and top-10 candidates. Reranker promotes the semantically closer but shorter doc that actually contains step-by-step commands.
[02:50] Riya: Nice — our problem is that long docs with the word 'TLS' but in an unrelated appendix are surfacing too high. Can rerank be biased toward anchors like section headers?
[03:05] Marco: Yes — you can pass metadata like section headers and weights; Console UI surfaces a relevance tuning slider for boosting certain fields. You can also fine-tune reranker weights via the config.
[03:20] Ben: Any support for vector stores? We currently use an internal Postgres + Annoy pipeline.
[03:26] Marco: We integrate with common vector DBs but the hosted flow doesn't require storing vectors in Redwood — you can send vectors to rerank directly, or we can host embeddings and provide a simple vector store middleware. For your existing infra you could keep using Postgres + Annoy and just call rerank as a second stage.
[03:46] Samir: What about payload size and rate limits? We batch a lot at night, spike during release cycles.
[03:52] Sofia: Hosted has quota tiers; for pilot we provide a temporary higher quota. Our console shows token usage and per-route cost breakdown so you can see where spikes occur.
[04:10] Marco: Now I'll flip to Console — show search tuning tab. You can upload your query set and label expected results; Console runs sampling and gives a relevance score and suggestions: field boosts, rerank threshold, and caching prefixes.
[04:38] Marco: The Optimize tab will recommend batching windows and quantization profiles based on observed sequence length distribution. For doc search typically we recommend 16-bit quant for embeddings indexing and 8-bit quant or FP16 for rerank.
[04:58] Olga: Does quantization impact quality? We can't tolerate regression >2% in our NDCG.
[05:05] Marco: We run regression tests against your eval set during model variant rollouts. Optimize also surfaces predicted quality impact; you can pin a non-quant variant for critical routes.
[05:25] Tara: Security: do you retain raw text? We need to be sure PII is not stored.
[05:31] Sofia: Hosted default retention is ephemeral for request payloads — you can enable longer retention for logs. We have SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations for customer-managed keys. We'll share the security pack.
[05:50] Riya: Is there an option to run rerank inside our VPC or customer-managed network?
[05:57] Marco: That's our Private deployment. For the pilot, we suggest hosted but if you need VPC peering or on-prem we can scope Redwood Private. It can increase setup time and cost.
[06:15] Ben: Latency numbers — can you share p50/p95 for rerank at 512 token contexts?
[06:22] Marco: For hosted with redwood-rerank-large at 512 tokens we typically see p50 ~80-110ms, p95 ~240-350ms depending on batch sizing. We'll include benchmark sheets.
[06:38] Sofia: We'll also provide a sample Jupyter notebook to run a live A/B between your current pipeline and reranker.
[06:45] Marco: Quick demo of running a relevance experiment: uploading labeled test set to Console, choosing baseline vs rerank, then Console computes NDCG, precision@5 and flags regressions.
[06:58] Riya: That eval flow looks great; how do we automate alerts on quality drift?
[07:06] Marco: Console has monitoring; you can set thresholds on the eval metrics or attach it to your CI to block model rollouts. Redwood Optimize can send alerts and snapshot diffs when regression >X%.
[07:20] Olga: Will the eval take into account our business metrics, like clicks->convert?
[07:25] Marco: You can surface custom metrics by uploading labels or conversion events as part of the eval set. We map those to composite scores.
[07:40] Tara: Pricing — how is rerank billed vs embeddings?
[07:43] Sofia: Embeddings billed per vector unit; rerank billed per candidate scored and per token for model compute. We'll share an estimator worksheet so you can feed in queries/day and average top-N to estimate monthly cost.
[07:58] Ben: For nightly re-indexing of 200k docs, any tips to reduce cost?
[08:04] Marco: Use prefix-based caching for stable content, incremental embeddings only for changed docs, and quantized indexes. Also schedule bulk jobs during off-peak to use burst capacity. Optimize will propose a config.
[08:22] Sofia: Ok, we'll pause demo and open to questions.
[08:26] Riya: One operational question — how do we debug mis-ranks in production?
[08:32] Marco: Console exposes per-request traces: we log retrieval score, rerank score, features used, and token-level attention snapshots (if enabled). You can link to traces from your app.
[08:46] Samir: Audit logs for compliance? We need immutable logs for 12 months.
[08:52] Sofia: That's part of our Enterprise package — audit retention add-on and export to your SIEM via S3 or syslog. We'll include that in the security pack.
[09:05] Ben: Any known gotchas migrating from BM25-only systems?
[09:10] Marco: Two things: candidate generation coverage (set top-N high enough so reranker has good options), and chunking strategy for long docs — chunk at semantic boundaries to avoid noisy partials. We provide chunking heuristics in the notebook.
[09:34] Tara: Could you run a quick live run on our sample corpus? (we had pre-shared a 500-doc subset).
[09:41] Marco: Sure — loading the dataset, running embeddings ingestion... (5-8s pause) ...embedding batch finished, running nearest neighbor retrieval, rerank on top-20.
[10:12] Marco: Results: baseline BM25 p@5 = 0.62, rerank pipeline p@5 = 0.78 on this sample. Caveat: small sample, but shows direction.
[10:28] Riya: That's promising. Curious about variance across query types.
[10:32] Marco: Console splits by query length and intent tags — short informational vs long procedural queries; rerank helps the long procedural ones most.
[10:45] Olga: Any limit on candidate list size for rerank?
[10:49] Marco: We have soft defaults at 100 candidates; reranking more increases cost linearly. Typically 20-50 is efficient.
[11:00] Sofia: Ok, quick recap and recommended pilot: 2-week hosted pilot, Redwood provides runner notebook + eval harness, customer provides 1k queries and a 10k doc corpus sample, we'll run daily evals and provide a dashboard.
[11:18] Riya: That works. We'll need SOC2 evidence and a data processing addendum before sending the sample.
[11:25] Sofia: We'll attach security docs and a DPA; Marco will include the benchmark sheet.
[11:35] Ben: One last question — are there pretrained rerank models tuned for documentation use-cases?
[11:40] Marco: We have variants optimized for docs and for e-commerce; Console recommends the docs variant when you upload a doc-style corpus. You can also fine-tune if you have labeled data.
[11:52] Tara: Great. Let's confirm next steps.
